newsitem.title: MEXICO: Lockheed Martin sees opportunity in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed Martin sees opportunity in Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's war on drugs, along with a spate of upcoming privatisations, have attracted companies to an aerospace trade show, seeking potentially lucrative contracts.
Among the companies vying for business at Aeroexpo '97, which runs through this weekend, is aerospace and high-tech giant Lockheed Martin Corp.

"There's been a move toward setting up primary radars on the west coast of Mexico so that narcotics traffickers coming up from South America will be visible," said John Rougas of Lockheed unit Ocean, Radar & Sensor Systems.
Rougas said the company's TPS-117 radar, which can be mounted on a truck, would be ideal for fighting the drug trade.
"We're very interested in pursuing the applications where a highly transportable radar like the TPS-117 is needed to ... counter narcotics trafficking," he said.
Rougas said the Mexican government was interested in such radars but conceded they cost "a lot of money."

With Mexican airports due to be sold off, Lockheed Martin will bid on some of those through its Airport Group International unit, which seeks to manage and operate airports throughout Latin America where other privatisations are also taking place.

Lockheed's Ocean, Radar & Sensor Systems will offer air traffic control systems and other hardware needed to improve the airports and also hopes to play a role in the privatisation of Mexican seaports.
Any day now, the government is due to publish a long-awaited programme for selling off its airports considered key to the privatisation process.
